author: chloecasey61
title: Best way to store photos!
review:
I’ve always been a huge picture person. I love saving memories from special moments and and even everyday life. I’ve had pictures stored in hundreds of files on my computer for years. When I downloaded google photos it automatically took all of those and downloaded them to the cloud. After the download was completed, I received the option to delete all the old photos from my computer, which made my life a lot easier. You can easily find a picture of someone specific you’re looking for and share pictures back and fourth with others using personal links! This app has a ton of great features, if you play around with it you can find a bunch of cool stuff you’re able to do! The one downside is that if you are using your personal gmail, there’s only 15 GB of storage. I have used all of googles apps for as long as I can remember so my storage was way over the 15 mark. I recently purchased 100 GB for $1.99 which I will hopefully not need anymore after I go through all my data linked from my gmail. Another downside is the download quality of images and especially videos. I have it set to upload at original quality so there’s not much else I can do. Just realize if you’re shooting a high quality video shoot it might not actually be able to be downloaded at the same quality.

Overall this is the best way to save pictures. I’ve been a google photos user for about 8 years now and I couldn’t be more pleased with this app. I’m a huge supporter of google photos and have got many of my friends hooked on its benefits too!

author: NevaehB22
title: Sneakiest app
review:
PLEASE READ BEFORE DOWNLOADING THIS APP
There is no way for me to unsync google photos/ refuse it access from my iPhone photos gallery. I cannot find anywhere in my settings to unsync/ refuse access. (And if you can it’s jumping through many hoops to get this parasite of an app of your back). There is also no place on the app to unsync your photos. There is only a place to turn off backup (which stops uploading your photos to google photos once you turn it off). I’ve been reading online forums, and reading other input elsewhere from many very outraged people, I found out that since I cannot unsync my photos first, if I delete any photos off of google photos, they will be permanently deleted from my iPhone and iCloud. This is insane and honestly should be illegal. As anyone else would be, I was under the impression that if I allow something access in settings, I can just turn it off later, like everything else I’ve downloaded. But no! I genuinely cannot find in my photos settings, google photos settings, and other settings, a way to refuse google photos access to my iPhone photos. Also, you can only select one photo at a time on google photos. So if you want to delete all of your photos off of there or move more than one to an album or something, you should probably have a lot of time on your hands! Please also be aware that if you delete something from your photos, even if you’ve emptied your trash, it will not delete off of google photos too. If anyone knows a way I can unsync google photos from my photos on my iPhone despite not having a way to from my settings, please lmk.

author: Goldy121
title: Wish All Assistants Were This Good!
review:
I have really enjoyed Google photos, especially for the assistant feature. Every now and then I’ll get a notification that the assistant has created a little movie or collage from pictures I took 2, 3, even 5 years ago. It’s great because it usually creates something that you’d like to have but you just never get around to making. Seeing old pictures of a trip with family and friends, the family pet doing something quirky, or being reminded of a special occasion can make your day. 

Candidly, I’m not a huge fan of the fact that Google has become this massive company with their hands in everything, but for utility apps like this there just aren’t many companies out there who have the time, money and imaginative software developers to create an app like this that actually makes it on to the App Store. For that reason I commend them. Now, if I could just figure out how to block every single move I make and web page I visit from them, I might just stop getting harassed by advertisements for things that I just searched for an hour ago on a completely different device connected to a completely different network!

author: EbCai
title: Reassuring
review: So let’s be honest. I was TERRIFIED of this app. Sounds crazy but it’s true. My iPhone kept telling me I was low on storage. And having an infant daughter it’s obvious that my pictures are the majority of the memory in my phone. Well. I had a dilemma. She’s so stinking cute that I neede to take pictures. More pictures. Lots of them. All the time. But I couldn’t! Not with no storage! So there I was. “To delete. Or not to delete.” I couldn’t decide what to do. Do I delete the pictures and pray that they’re backed up to google photos? Or do I delete them from my photos and risk the chance of losing all 7mo of her life caught on camera? Well after two days of deliberating and asking questions on Facebook, I decided to open the google photos app. And lo and behold, “Assistant” popped up. And do you know what Assistant said? It said “your phone storage is very low. Would you like to make space?” So of course I wanted to make space. I needed to know how “Assistant” over here planned in doing it. So I clicked it. And the next prompt notified me that x amount of pictures had been downloaded and backed up to the google photos app and that all I needed to do was press a button to delete them. I let out the biggest sigh of relief knowing that choosing to delete those pictures from my phone didn’t mean permanent loss. They simply just relocated! So I clicked it again and let it happen! All I had to do from there was open up my OLD photos app and clear out my “recently deleted” folder. It’s still got 642 pictures left to backup and delete. But I’m going to sleep wonderfully knowing that while I’m in this WiFi, my google photos app is making it easy for me to document my daughters life and not compromising the use of my phone to do it. Shout out to Google Photos. This app is the bombbbbb!

author: smmrsvr
title: Batch-Archive Only? How About Batch-Deleting?
review:
Can’t beat the price, and the fact that they’ll hardly go out of business like PhotoBucket did — and my old photos with it. Now I would like Google Photos to give me the option to either batch-archive or batch-delete on the same screen when they remind me of the memes and document snapshots I have in storage. That’s the user-intuitive way. They want me to batch-archive so that’s what they offer, and I end up storing a lot of junk since I have both WhatsApp and GP set to sync with my phone storage app (I want to keep the photos my family sends, but with it come memes, viral videos etc). I don’t have the time at the end of the day to go through both storage apps deleting the junk.

Another thing is they didn’t keep up to date with the news when they suggested an album to be titled “Trip USA-Canada” in Aug’21 just bc we took pictures in the American boat in Niagara Falls. Canada’s borders were closed to Americans due to the pandemic; and the only photos of Canada I had were taken from the boat looking up to the buildings right on the borders—by all measures a stretch to call it a Canada trip.

author: SuiPhx83
title: Take me to that date
review:
Feature Request:

I’ve got years and years of photos uploaded with you.  When I search for a photo and you give me a result, I often want to review the rest of the photos taken from that date.  Currently to do so you have to back out and manually scroll through to the year, month and day or do another search for that month and year but then still scroll through to the moments to get around to the ‘time’ you’re looking for.  It seems weird that you cannot access the photos from a particular date from the already populated search results.  

I request that from the info of a photo that you’ve searched, that the date stamp be a hyperlink that takes you to the rest of the photos from that date.  Basically to your normal view/feed of your photos (such that you could scroll earlier or later if you wished) but by clicking the date you can go to all the photos taken at that time and not have to perform another search/operation to get there.

author: JKlutz
title: Couldn’t live without it
review:
Seriosuly Google Photos is a MUST for any sentimental human. I want to find a photo from something I did years ago? Can’t remember what year it even was? No problem. I can type in the location, or I can type in a key term like, “Renaissance faire” or “pizza” I don’t know, anything, and it’ll pull up related photos for me. I can usually find what I’m looking for quickly and I also discover some other forgotten gems in the process. 
I love that it has facial recognition, so I can easily narrow my searches down by people or pets. I also have albums for each of my kids that are automatically updated with photos containing their faces, without me having to do anything. I also automatically share these photos with family and friends. They get to see all of the kids photos/videos and all o have to do is take the picture. They automatically get backed up from my iPhone and automatically added to albums and automatically shared… I mean… how could I not use this?
Also, we recently discovered a new perk: partner sharing! My husband and I turned on partner sharing to share photos with each other so we no like get have to trade phones and airdrop yo each other haha.

Oh! And years ago I had Google photos back up my Facebook albums. Remember the mid 2000s when we would upload like 86 photos to a Facebook album? Well those are on Google now and I could delete them from Facebook. So yet another perk.

Anyway, clearly I highly recommend this. Been using it for years. No complaints.

author: frozzle85
title: Lost photos/videos because the sync doesn’t work
review:
When my phone got stolen, I lost so many photos and videos that were on my google photos app on my iphone but weren’t on my google photos Web. I was missing photos and videos on the web version that spanned months, while my Google Photos app on my phone had everything to the most recent day. But I never recovered those pictures on Google Photos. Thank goodness for iCloud, otherwise I would’ve lost all of those pictures over the several months that Google Photos did not sync. 

Before my phone was stolen, Back up and sync were turned on prior. Backups were allowed over cellular data. So why did my photos from the past several months not sync automatically and quickly to google photos Web? Even now, they don’t sync until I log into Google photos web? Please fix so we don’t have to worry about losing memories when something happens to our phones. The syncing doesn’t always work and even now with my new phone I notice a huge lag in the syncing to the web version. The lag needs to be significantly reduced or eliminated because why should I pay for extra storage and it won’t actually sync anything?

author: holco121
title: Great app
review: I’m so impressed with this app! I had a nightmare trying to save all my iPhone photos from my phone to my laptop. The USB cable wouldn’t connect properly, iCloud didn’t have enough storage and it was taking ageeesss to upload all of the 1500 photos/videos I had. I then downloaded Google Photos and it’s worked perfectly. I downloaded the app on my phone and the photos uploaded so much quicker than iCloud. I then downloaded the photos on my laptop using the Google Photos website. Next, I deleted the 1500 photos from my iPhone so I could save storage on my phone and I’m really pleased to say that the Google Photos app has kept all my old photos as well as it’s been adding new ones I’ve been taking. author: Bottay
title: Saved me!
review:
I lost 7000 photos and videos from my iPhone when it suddenly had a blip. I’d been paying for the iCloud and was sure it had backed up. Devastatingly, it hadn’t and all was lost. I heard about google photos app and decided to download it. That was 4 years ago and I’ve never looked back! I tell all my friends and family to do the same. I love the convenience of it and how you only have to simply “open” the app in order for it to backup all the videos and photos on your iPhone. I love how google makes videos and animations with them too! There’s been some really lovely creations! It’s so easy to find a photo just by looking for the date or a keyword for it. The face recognition has saved me so much scrolling time too!
Thank you google pics!!

author: Hoo Niko
title: Tried it, don’t like it, regret using it
review:
Long story short: think twice before you use this app, you’ll loose lots of cool functionalities like map search (iPhone) and reverting is actually complicated

iPhone user: In fact google photo at first makes it look like a great idea, it’s seamless to synchronize your photos from iPhone to the app. 

However, when you want to see your photos, if you don’t have a good internet connection it doesn’t work, most apps wanting to upload photos won’t recognize google photo but only the album from the actual iPhone, so if they’re removed from your original photos gallery then you have to find them and download them again, you loose the map view that iPhone has to place your photo where you took them (which is actually very convenient to quickly find a photo)

Now, the worst part in my opinion, I want to revert that, stop using google photos and remove the app, but there no easy way to do that now, some photos are on both apps, some are only on one, some only on the other, that’s going to get messy to rebalance years of photos in one place with duplicates and all.

author: Dan_Evo_P

If you love looking back at memories, get this!

author: MaccaTed
title: Not just backup
review:

Also like the suggestions for changes, suggested panoramas from shots that I took in quick succession.

author: Maritime Rose
title: Was Terrific
review: Google Photos no longer works properly on my iPad Pro.  I cannot edit photos, I cannot delete photos and I cannot find my many albums created over the years, they are gone.  I cannot share albums.  It works fine on my iphone pro 14.  I loved it, but now I’m so disappointed.

author: J37748595996
title: Nonsensical Product Limitations
review:
Why can't this app search for photos that aren't backed up to the google cloud? All the data is on my phone.

Fire whoever made this illogical decision and have a good discussion about what a bad direction your products have been going in.

author: yeikwn w
title: LOST PHOTOS
review: I backed up everything properly and I'm now missing the whole month of august, photos of a concert, lots of memories with friends like camping, all of its just gone. Thanks google!

author: AcrossTheMelody
title: Beware of Photo Deletions
review: I used to love Google Photos, but one day they deleted a lot of my old photo albums without informing me that they would do so—presumably to free up space once the 15GB free limit was imposed.  I lost a lot of very precious photos that I do not have physical backups of, as I placed far too much trust in Google for my photo backups.  It is otherwise a great app, but I wish the company were more transparent about its photo deletion practices.

author: Manvir mahey
title: Keep lagging
review: Whenever i am trying to access my old pictures app keeps freezing. I can do nothing when going back to old pics. I’m using this app since 2018 and there’s no way to be back my old memories and data. Its disgusting 😬
